headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Botpress can install packages while marketingskills can read/write files, spawn subprocesses, and use allowlisted network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented shared channel, but marketingskills explicitly uses shared skill files and shared context, so if Botpress outputs are copied into those files or prompts, instruction injection becomes plausible. The pair lacks a proven direct bridge, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into marketingskills skill files or prompts, injection risk materializes.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep Botpress and marketingskills in separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or file-based handoff between agents.
Require a human review step before marketingskills consumes Botpress output.
Add a prompt delimiter and provenance tag to all Botpress outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing for shared skill files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress touches no data classes in the profile, while marketingskills reads and writes files and calls external APIs. If sensitive content is placed in the shared files marketingskills uses, it can be transmitted outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in .agents/skills or .claude/skill files, marketingskills can read it.
IF marketingskills sends those files or derived context to GitHub or marketing-skills.com, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or customer data in shared skill files.
Restrict marketingskills to a redacted workspace.
Review outbound API calls before enabling them.
Rotate any credentials that may already be present in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on file reads and API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and marketingskills can write the filesystem, read files, spawn subprocesses, and use allowlisted network egress. That overlap creates a default conflict surface around shared directories, dependency changes, and subprocess side effects; marketingskills also supports multiple instances, increasing race risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, package or file races can occur.
IF marketingskills runs multiple instances against shared state, conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Lock dependency installation behind a single operator-controlled step.
Disable concurrent marketingskills instances on shared state.
Use read-only mounts for Botpress where possible.
requires-engineering: add file and package locks around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around skills that reference each other and build on shared context, so it may treat Botpress output as authoritative if handed over directly. Botpress can generate content but has no documented verification layer here; the pair therefore has a plausible unverified-to-authoritative cascade, though not a proven action-taking chain.
conditions: IF Botpress output is inserted into marketingskills shared context without review, downstream errors can propagate.
IF marketingskills uses that context to draft marketing assets, factual mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations before marketingskills reuses Botpress output.
Mark Botpress output as untrusted input in prompts.
Limit marketingskills to drafting, not final publication.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no residency or retention constraints shown, while marketingskills exposes file paths and external APIs but no explicit compliance mismatch. Because no concrete jurisdictional or retention conflict is documented, only a low, gap-based compliance concern is justified.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into marketingskills files or APIs, compliance review is required.
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention behavior, policy mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared files.
Review retention settings for external APIs.
Document which agent may store which data class.
Keep audit logs of file and API access.
requires-engineering: add explicit retention and residency controls.
